description: Explains the top-of-atmosphere and surface energy budgets, albedo, greenhouse radiation, forcing and feedback, ocean thermal inertia, and how CERES and ocean observations constrain Earth’s energy imbalance.

related_resources.reason: Incoming shortwave, reflected albedo, outgoing infrared, global versus surface budgets; educational overview and approximate climatological numbers.
Present-day energy flows; feedbacks including water vapor, cloud, ice and radiative forcing; uncertainty and ocean heat uptake.
Satellite observations of reflected solar and emitted thermal radiation; calibration and energy-budget interpretation.
Argo history, measurement depths, global temperature/salinity profiles and Deep Argo development.
CERES-based Earth radiation budget and documented positive recent energy imbalance; particular values are time-dependent.

background: Uses only everyday energy and temperature concepts; radiation wavelength, conservation, and feedback are explained in the lecture.
readiness_checks: Why is a surface energy balance different from a top-of-atmosphere balance?
How does an infrared-absorbing atmosphere emit radiation rather than simply block it?
Why does ocean heat storage matter when satellite fluxes are measured at the top of the atmosphere?
Why can water vapor act as a feedback while carbon dioxide acts as a forcing?
